senses.definition: A type of perfume consisting of 2–5% essential oils, 70–90% alcohol and water.
examples: You stink of too much cologne.

quotes.text: The perfume market has always been a two-tiered one, with a relatively small number of buyers of small bottles of real perfume and eau de parfum that cost large amounts of money, and a larger number of buyers of somewhat larger bottles of cologne and eau de toilette that are considerably more affordable but not always cheap.
quotes.reference: 1987 October, Timothy Kalich, “Marketing: What's in a Smell?”, in The Atlantic, →ISSN:

quotes.text: He wore some aftershave or cologne that gave him a heavy, nasty, sweet scent.
quotes.reference: 1998, Octavia E. Butler, Parable of the Talents, HEADLINE PUBLISHING GROUP (2019), page 95:

senses.definition: Any of a family of fresh, citrus-based fragrances distilled using extracts from citrus, floral, and woody ingredients, said to have been developed in the early 18th century in Cologne, Germany.
(loosely) A fragrance typically worn by a man as opposed to a woman, regardless of its concentration.
